answer: Each new identity locks a terrace custody bond and receives one unique data shard from the terrace catalogue, signed under its kernel key. Verifiers issue random retrieval challenges; a hollow answer, missing or copied, burns the bond. Bond rises by terrace tier: the first hundred pay 80 credits each, each later hundred pays 5 more, so the 1,000th pays 125 and 1,000 fakes lock 102,500 credits. A rented shard fails because its kernel signature differs from the applicant key, and duplicate shard hashes are rejected. An honest agent locks one bond once and recovers it on passing.
